slides.title: Cartilage
slides.english_text:
Cartilage
⚫ 2 main types of cartilages:
⚫ Articular(hyaline) cartilage
⚫ Covers the articulating ends of the bones in the free moving joints
⚫ Function:
⚫ Transit compressive forces across the joint
⚫ Allows motion in the joint with minimal friction
⚫ Redistributes contact stresses over a larger area
⚫ Protects underlying bones
⚫ Fibrocartilage
⚫ Acts as an intermediary between hyaline cartilage and other connective tissues
⚫ Can withstand high pressures
⚫ Refers to as articular disc, or meniscus

slides.title: Ligaments

Ligaments
⚫ Short bands of tough fibrous connective tissue that binds bones to bones
⚫ Provides support in one direction, and often blends with the capsule of the joint

⚫ Extracapsular ligaments: outside the joint
⚫ Intra-articular ligaments: located inside the joint
⚫ Function:
⚫ Guide normal joint movement
⚫ Restrict abnormal joint movement

slides.title: Role of Muscle
slides.english_text:
Role of Muscle
⚫ Developing Torque
⚫ A muscle controls or creates a movement through the development of torque
⚫ Torque: the tendency of a force (tension) to produce rotation about a specific axis (the joint)
⚫ The amount of tension is influenced by the angle of attachment of the muscle
⚫ Muscle Actions creating, opposing, and stabilizing movements
⚫ In one movement of a joint, e.g. shoulder abduction
⚫ Agonists: muscles creating the movement
⚫ Antagonists: muscles opposing or producing the opposite joint movement
⚫ Stabilizers & Neutralizers: muscles contracting to eliminate the undesired joint action of another muscle
